sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:176031
Court No. - 66

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 41178 of 2024
Applicant :- Indrapal Singh Yadav

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Puneet Bhadauria
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Sri Anurag Shukla, learned Advocate filed his power on behalf of the informant, today in the
Court, which is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Puneet Bhadauria, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Anurag Shukla, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Vijay Kumar, learned AGA-I for the State.
3.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 307 of 2023, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 504, 506, 427, 120B, 34 IPC and 2/3 Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act, 1984, Police Station Friends Colony, District Etawah during pendency of the trial.

sentences.text: 4. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and others and according to the FIR on the basis of fake and forged document, applicant sold the property to the co-accused, which was allocated for the purpose of public way.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that on the basis of false allegation, applicant has been made accused in the present matter.
He further submits that actually property in question belongs to the applicant and applicant sold his own property.

6. He next submits even before lodgment of the FIR, informant of the case filed a civil suit for permanent injunction against applicant and co-accused Vinod Badauria, in which, she could not get any interim order and suit filed by her is still pending and plaint of the same has been annexed at page-130 of the paper-book, therefore, prima facie, it appears to be a case of civil dispute.
He next submits, who is owner of the property can only be decided by the competent civil court.

7. He next submits that however proceedings under Section 133 Cr.P.C. initiated on the application moved by the informant is pending against the applicant but State has not taken any action against the applicant.

8. He further submits, however, earlier applicant was made accused in as many as 14 other cases but in eight cases after investigation final report has been submitted and in three cases he has already been acquitted and his criminal history has been explained in the instant bail application.

9. He further submits that all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate and in the present matter applicant is in jail since 05.09.2024 i.e. for last two months.
10.

Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted, applicant is the person, who by playing fraud even sold the property, which was allocated for the purpose of public way and he is also having criminal history of 14 other cases but they could not dispute the fact that with regard to property in question before lodgment of the FIR,
informant filed a civil suit for permanent injunction against the applicant, which is still pending.
They further could not dispute the fact that out of 14 cases in eight cases final report has been submitted and in three cases applicant has been acquitted.
11. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the informant however further submits that after submission of the final report, in one case applicant has been summoned on the basis of protest petition.
12. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

13. However, as per allegation applicant by playing fraud sold the property, which was allocated for the purpose of public way to co-accused Vinod Bhadauria but it reflects with regard to property in question civil suit is pending between informant and applicant, which was filed by the informant herself.

14. Further, however, apart from the present case applicant is having criminal history of 14 other cases but in eight cases final report has been submitted and in three cases applicant has already been acquitted.

sentences.text: Further, all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate and in the present matter applicant is in jail since 05.09.2024 i.e. for last two months.

16. Further, law is settled that bail should not be refused for punitive purpose and bail is a rule while bail rejection is an exception.
17.

Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
18. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

19. Let the applicant - Indrapal Singh Yadav be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
20.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

21. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
Order Date :- 11.11.2024 AK Pandey  Indrapal Singh Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172789217/
